item.title: Learning on your own
item.description: Words for studying by yourself, building habits and tracking your progress.

children.definition: the feeling of wanting to do something and the energy to do it
children.example: Having a clear goal gives me motivation to study every day.

children.definition: the process of getting better at something over time
children.example: I can see real progress in my listening since January.

children.definition: something you do often and regularly, almost without thinking
children.example: Reading ten pages before bed has become a good habit.

children.definition: something that takes your attention away from what you are doing
children.example: My phone is my biggest distraction when I study.

children.definition: to give all your attention to one thing
children.example: I find it easier to focus in the library than at home.

children.definition: to decide on something you want to achieve
children.example: I set a goal to learn twenty new words every week.

children.definition: a small card with a word on one side and its meaning on the other
children.example: I use flashcards on the bus to review vocabulary.

children.definition: able to speak a language easily and well
children.example: After a year in Germany, she became fluent in German.

children.definition: to do something again and again so you get better at it
children.example: I practise speaking with a friend on video calls.

children.definition: to stop trying to do something because it is difficult
children.example: Don't give up just because the first month is hard.

children.definition: to make sure you know what is happening or how much you have done
children.example: I keep track of my study time in a small notebook.

children.definition: having learned a skill by yourself, without a teacher
children.example: He's a self-taught programmer who learned from free online courses.
